summary: Re-verified against the tree, not the account. The round-12 F1 fix holds: every javadoc site the notes name resolves and both named blind spots are real -- Sequencer.java:35/:46/:48-50/:88, CommitRequest.java:19 and :35-36 ('@param flushSeq ... Together with {@code podId} it identifies this commit uniquely across the fleet'), FakeSequencer.java:27/:29, FakeSequencerTest.java:178, Checkpoint.java:32 (format/, the (podId, flushSeq)-from-M4.1 clause), IngestCommitPathTest.java:81, CommitProtocolSimulation.java:58, CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest.java:23. The three SPEC sites now cited by text each resolve uniquely and each does say (podId, flushSeq): SPEC.md:55 'from the outset', :508 'The multi-pod gap becomes invisible', :518 the M4.1 row. The ADR's tree claims re-checked and true: golden chain-delta-batched-v1.bin holds bins/a.seg and bins/b.seg; BatchingSequencerTest:259-261 is from(pod0,0)/from(pod1,0) with hasSize(2); :93/:152 are new CommitRequest("pod"+pod, 0, ...); Checkpoint.decode is version != VERSION; CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest:117 is bytes[7]=1; CheckpointTest:169 is < 64*1024 with the ~38 KiB comment at :158; MAX_KEY_BYTES is 1024; CheckpointWriter:129 is pods.merge(request.podId(), request.flushSeq(), Math::max); DefaultIngest:349 evaluates flushSeq++ as the commit argument and flushLocked discards `published` on failure; ChainReplay's Hop javadoc :50 says 'never GET at all' and applyChain does LIST from the seeded checkpoint. The F2 fix is NOT landable as staged: the clause was inserted as a SECOND acceptance criterion numbered 9 rather than folded into criterion 9, which defeats the only script that enumerates criteria (measured), and criterion 6's new absolute clause is false for the one failure the feature exists for. Two majors, three minors.

findings.title: The replay-answering bound is a SECOND criterion numbered 9, and check-milestone-verified.sh cannot tell the two apart
findings.failure_scenario: The acceptance-criteria list now holds two items numbered '9.' -- :443 (the replay-answering GET) and :447 (commit cost does not scale with pods or streams). check-milestone-verified.sh extracts criteria with `re.findall(r'^\s*(-?\d+)\.\s+(.+)$')` and then, per criterion, searches VERIFIED.md for `^\s*<n>\.\s+`. MEASURED on the staged file: it finds 13 criteria numbered ['1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8','9','9','10','11','12'], and a VERIFIED.md carrying ONE line per distinct number reports `missing: []`. So at M4.15 a single '9. asserted by LocalSequencerCommitCostTest' evidence line discharges BOTH -- the pod-axis GET criterion added this round to stop being prose can be omitted from M4's VERIFIED.md with the gate green. That gate's stated purpose is 'it forces ENUMERATION, which catches the quiet omission', and this is the quiet omission. Two further consequences: (a) five existing citations of 'criterion 9' now resolve to two different criteria -- SPEC.md:370 ('Acceptance criterion 9 asserts the pod dimension specifically'), SPEC.md:508, and ADR-0032:15, :75, :90, all of which mean the PUT criterion; (b) markdown renumbers an ordered list from its first item, so the rendered document has no criterion 9 at all where those citations point -- the PUT criterion renders as 10, and 10/11/12 as 11/12/13. ⚠️ The fix is NOT to renumber (that breaks the five citations); it is to fold the clause into criterion 9's own text as the preceding clause it is written to be -- its opening words, 'AND NOR DOES THE REPLAY-ANSWERING GET', already have no antecedent where it sits, since the item above it is the failover-time criterion and the 'nor' points at the item BELOW.

findings.title: 'THE POINTER IS RECORDED FOR EVERY APPLIED COMMIT ... ALWAYS answered' is false for the ambiguous PUT that landed -- the case idempotency exists for
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 6 now asserts without qualification that the pointer is recorded for EVERY applied commit and that a replay of a pod's most recent applied flushSeq is ALWAYS answered, the refuse branch applying 'only BELOW that watermark'. The tree cannot deliver that on the one path that produces replays today. LocalSequencer.java:346-354 calls `log.commitAll(requests)` and only then, on normal return, `writer.observe(requests)` -- and CheckpointWriter:129 is where the per-pod watermark is set. An IOException from the chain PUT is defined by Sequencer.java:43-45 as the AMBIGUOUS case: 'a conditional PUT whose response was lost has still landed'. In that case the commit IS applied (the delta is in the chain, the offsets are consumed) and the pointer/watermark is NOT recorded -- observe never ran. The pod then retries the same (podId, incarnationId, flushSeq); the ADR says detection is 'an in-memory comparison against state recovered once per takeover', so nothing detects it, no pointer is consulted, and the sequencer assigns a SECOND offset range to records that already hold one. That is I2, and it is the exact harm ADR-0036 opens by naming. Nothing downstream catches it: neither the ADR, nor backlog.md's M4.10d row, nor the #m410d notes mention the landed-but-thrown commit, and every M4 fixture commits successfully, so an M4.10d that records the pointer in `observe` and tests a replay after a SUCCESSFUL commit satisfies criterion 6 as written, satisfies the T0 row, and ships a dedup that is a no-op against ambiguity. Either the criterion must say which commits are 'applied' for its purposes and hand the landed-but-thrown one to a named row, or it must state that the retry path folds what it lost the race to -- a mechanism nothing in this diff describes. As staged it is the round-12 F1 shape again: a sentence certifying its own completeness ('EVERY', 'ALWAYS') over a set it has not checked.

findings.title: 'which cost.md permits' licenses the pod axis from a list pods are not on
findings.failure_scenario: The Consequences concede one GET per replaying pod when pointers name different deltas and justify it as scaling 'with replaying nodes, which cost.md permits'. cost.md's invariant lists segments, AZs and nodes as permitted and records, shards, partitions, indices, documents as forbidden -- pods appear on NEITHER list, which this repository has already established: the staged baselines/review.txt entry `rounds:M4.10` records that a citation of cost.md R6 was deleted because 'pods appear on no rule's list, so no citation was available and the bullet now states the tree fact instead'. Meanwhile SPEC.md:368-370 says flatly 'Nothing may make the commit rate scale with records, shards, partitions, indices -- or **pods**', and the M4.10b row's own property is 'no COMMIT-PATH request that scales with the number of pods', with a retry path explicitly in scope ('Resolving a replay by walking the chain backwards is the same fault in GETs'). The concrete harm is downstream reading: an M4.10d session takes 'cost.md permits one GET per replaying pod' as settled, issues a GET per replaying pod without coalescing on the pointer, and only the shared-pointer case is pinned by the T0 row. Say the tree fact instead -- each GET fetches a DISTINCT object, so it is per-object not per-pod, and the coalescing bound is what makes the shared case one -- rather than asserting a permission cost.md does not give.

findings.title: The new T0 row is a relative assertion with no floor: zero GETs passes it
findings.failure_scenario: 'GET count per `commitAll` unchanged from 1 replaying pod to 6 when their pointers share one delta' is satisfied by 0 == 0. A dedup that always REFUSES a detected replay -- never reading the pointed delta at all -- issues no GETs at either pod count and passes this row with its named mutation ('N GETs of one shared delta') dead for the wrong reason. The anti-vacuity lives only in criterion 6's prose, and the test plan is what an implementer writes tests from. This repository has already paid for exactly this: M4.8b2's `seq = nextSequence() - 1` mutant 'survived because every assertion was relative'. One clause fixes it -- EXACTLY one GET, not merely an equal count.

findings.title: The row is tiered T0 while counting store requests through commitAll
findings.failure_scenario: testing.md's tier table gives T0 'backing store: none' and puts MemoryBinStore at T1; cost.md rule 9 counts store operations through CountingBinStore, which decorates a store. A GET count per `commitAll` cannot be observed without one, which is why the sibling row directly above it -- 'Commit batching: PUT count unchanged from 1 pod to 6 and 1 stream to 1,000' -- is T1, as is 'Bounded recovery ... caught by request count'. Tiers map to Gradle tasks (build.md), so a mis-tiered row either lands in the wrong task or pushes an implementer following testing.md rule 1 ('default to T0') to assert on an in-memory counter inside the dedup instead of on real store requests -- and an in-memory counter cannot see a GET issued from anywhere else on the commit path, which is the whole point of counting at the store.
